confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors are based on three web searches: one for the RBA rate and two for Mendoza prices. The price figures come from crowd-sourced cost-of-living sites (Wise, Nomads, Expatistan, CityCost, Livingcost) and a 2026 Mendoza nightlife guide. Those sources disagree a lot. A dinner for two ranged from about USD 11 to USD 40, a cappuccino from about USD 4.4 to USD 5.1, and a 0.5 L beer from about USD 2 to USD 4. The peso also moves fast, so USD prices can shift within weeks. I used middle values and adjusted them to a standard serving. The cocktail figure comes from the nightlife guide's AR$7,000-15,000 range, taking the lower to middle part. I found no recent, consistent figure for wine by the glass. I set it slightly above beer, because local Malbec is plentiful and house wine is cheap, while tourist wine bars charge more. Wine and cocktails are less certain than the coffee and meal figures. All four accommodation anchors are my own estimates from general knowledge. I did not search for them or look at any booking pages. They assume July demand from winter holidays and nearby ski trips, and they are the least certain of the ten.
comparable_city_reasoning: Based mainly on Mendoza-specific aggregated price data. I checked the results against other Argentine tourist cities with similar demand, such as Córdoba and Salta, and against Buenos Aires prices, which are somewhat higher. Argentina's USD prices have risen sharply since 2024, so I treated it as a mid-priced Latin American destination rather than a cheap one.
